core_obligations: Reduce modulo the powers of the ideal (proof lines 5853-5857): by the comparison lemma each reduction F/I^n F is the pullback of a locally constant sheaf G_n of Lambda/I^n-modules, and since X is connected each G_n is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf on a finite module M_n.

Analyse on a covering by weakly contractible pieces (proof lines 5857-5863): choose a covering of X by affine weakly contractible schemes W_t; on such a piece the restriction of F satisfies the hypotheses of the cited computation lemma, so F restricted to W_t is the completion of a finite module N_t over the completion of Lambda.

Compare the pieces (proof lines 5863-5868): the reduction of N_t modulo I^n is M_n for every t and n, so the completed modules N_t have isomorphic completions and hence, by the algebra lemma for finite modules over a Noetherian ring, are all isomorphic; therefore F is locally isomorphic to the completion of a single finite module, that is, F is adic lisse.
proof_roadmap: Use the comparison with the etale site and connectedness to identify the reductions up to locally constant finite modules.
Use a covering by affine weakly contractible schemes and the local description of lisse constructible sheaves there.
Compare the finitely many resulting modules through their reductions and conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a connected scheme X, a Noetherian ring Lambda and an ideal I, every lisse constructible Lambda-sheaf on the pro-etale site of X is adic lisse (statement lines 5845-5851). The proof (proof lines 5853-5871) identifies the reductions with pullbacks of locally constant etale sheaves, restricts to a covering by affine weakly contractible schemes where the sheaf is the completion of a finite module, and concludes by comparing those modules through their reductions and completions. H2: a three-step argument with five inputs, written out in full.
